answer: Persistent trail ledger. Each identity must solve a unique random challenge whose output seeds a walk through a shared state graph; two identities landing on the same vertex must publish a distinguishing cipher proving separate work. Duplicate keys collapse into one karst-like sink and forfeit accumulated history. An attacker cloning N agents pays N full challenge computations plus lost registration history per duplicate, making mass duplication costlier than honest enrollment and detectable on collision.
